# Chapter Three: Corliss

> *"A time for love, a time for hate, a time for peace and a time for war."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

The discreet blonde sat silently at a table in the far corner of the small village inn. Pipe smoke hung heavy in the air like a thick fog permeating the ancient timbers that encircled the customers giving the inn a memorable smell she would soon not forget the woman thought crinkling her nose.

The patrons covertly shot suspicious glances and whispers in her direction, sky blue eyes and a firmly set alabaster jaw stood partially hidden under a large leather bolero hat, the scuffs and stains told of hard use.

The woman sat poised, back straight and body tense, the only motion was the lifting of a dented and scraped tin cup as it disappeared for a moment under the hat only to quickly reemerge, coming back to rest on the table with a light clink.

Sitting there she could continue to hear the whispers and felt the curious stares as the intensity of the patron’s gazes sent the hairs on the back of her neck to attention.

Corliss heard the uncomfortable shifting of bodies as the old wooden chairs groaned in protest, still using the leather brim as cover, her eyes roved over the room assessing the collection of pistols, swords and other assorted items that peaked from under jackets and along worn leather belts as the customers shifted position so, not all soldiers, she thought trying to ascertain which was which.

The inn was walking distance to the local barracks and would be frequented by the soldiers of the crown and of the Lord Seer.

The long bastard swords with their black hilts marked these men and she dismissed them readily, they would pose no threat, she had her royal seal allowing her to work as a warden and they would respect it, however the other patrons would not be so readily swayed she mused still looking over those with weapons that would be considered unorthodox as she spotted filed down scythes and deer antlers.

This was a local tavern, not a place where strangers were seen often, when one arrived, they quickly became the object of speculation and suspicion.

Corliss understood this, she had been in more than her fair share of local taverns brought here by duty just as was the case this night, reaching out with finely tuned senses her ears joined the work of her eyes, listening intently for anyone trying to approach, slowly she lowered one hand under the table running a finger along the worn leather of the large belt she wore around her thin waist, fingers were soon rewarded as they found the set of leather tassels, smiling and with practiced ease she loosened the ties that held the two pistols in place, allowing them to be drawn quickly should the need arise.

This is looking more and more like a gun fight she thought bitterly as her mind counted the number of firearms in the tavern. Her breath hitched as the sound of the Tavern’s door opened her eyes now drawn to the large wooden opening as the new patron stepped in from the cold.

Corliss tensed as her eyes followed the young man hesitantly entering the establishment. He was a large lad with shoulder length dark hair and an earnest face, his dark eyes wide as he shot nervous glances around the room the patrons turning to regard him with suspicion and a trace of hostility.

The burgundy dragon tattoo on his cheek marked him as a mage and looking around the tavern Corliss could see the glances of mistrust and resentment that greeted the young man.

She had always felt bad for the mages, their abilities separating them from the people, they spent their lives in service, never trusted and never welcome she thought, but there had been a time when all of these people’s great grandfathers would have had that same power, so was it mistrust or was it jealousy she mused, watching intently as the man quickly crossed the bar and took a place at a corner table away from the crowd of patrons.

Part of the world but always separate she thought a small trace of sadness flitting through her mind. She regarded the mage and lost in thought Corliss almost missed the door opening a second time, the long creak as the hinges protesting their use her only warning.

The intelligent blue eyes disappeared under the brim as a distinct and familiar set of footfalls made their way across the dirty wooden planks a thump followed by a scrape and then repeated.

Corliss knew the sound in fact she had been the one to cause the limp that gave the man that distinct gate, a wicked smile spreading across her face as she recalled the incident.

The large brim still hiding her face, she first looked down at the floor watching the old worn boots pass the table, the left leg dragging causing that scraping sound to the man’s gate.

Corliss carefully reached down and unwrapped the piece of leather tied to the two hatchets along the back of her belt making the weapons readily available.

Waiting as the man’s odd gate continued towards the bar Corliss shifted allowing her an easy exit from the table, she hunched her shoulders giving her more of a subservient look, it was her ability to hide in plain sight that had garnered her the nickname Ghost within the ranks of the wardens, the crippled man passed without giving her a second look, not even noticing the smile spread across her face as he passed.

With a sigh of resignation Corliss removed the hat revealing high cheekbones and those sky-blue eyes framed over a generous mane of long blonde hair tied back in a tight ponytail.

The look on her face would turn any man’s blood cold as she stared down the men around her each set of eyes dropping to the floor as they met hers. Standing she stretched her back and cracked her neck, knowing what was coming and not looking forward to it.

“Castigan Morinth, you are a fugitive of the crown and are bound by law to accompany me to the city of Lester for trial, do you concede?”

She bellowed as Corliss announced her presence. The tavern grew quiet as all eyes snapped to regard the female Warden and then slowly, every eye in the place drifted to the crippled man standing by the old bar.

The man, just a little taller than Corliss stood there, his brown floor-length coat rustled across the worn wood floor as he turned to reveal a dark brooding face, a prominent scar from the two’s last encounter ran along the man’s cheek the white of the scar a contrast to his Mediterranean coloring, short black hair and deep brown eyes.

A smile spread across his face revealing a mouth full of discolored and crooked teeth.

“Corliss how is it you found me this time” the words oozing out of his mouth like a vile sludge. Castigan was the worst of the worst, aside from the six murders he was wanted for, he had left a wake of rape, assault and theft over three territories and every time Corliss had failed in bringing him to justice.

But not this time, this time she had caught up to Castigan. Of the six murders he was wanted for, two of them had been fellow Wardens and one had been a close friend.

Corliss wanted Castigan to refuse, wanted him to resist, “It wasn’t easy Castigan, but I am here, will you submit to my authority” she asked and for a moment felt disappointment as the man’s shoulders slumped and Corliss thought he would surrender. But that had only been a feint, suddenly Castigan tensed, the two soldiers to his right began to pull their pistols.

Corliss was faster her hands a blur as the guns quickly appeared, the hammers snapping down, as a bright blue explosion of energy hit the first one in the shoulder and the second one in the gut, “dammit” she whispered she should have anticipated he would have had friends she chided herself.

Stepping forward she dropped the pistols, she wanted Castigan alive, her hands disappearing behind her back and then coming back out with two midnight hatchets just in time to see Castigan level his own pistol at her.

With only a second to decide Corliss threw the first hatchet at the man, causing him to duck left to avoid it. But it was a long enough pause for the Warden to take two steps, swiping the gun off its target with the edge of the second hatchet as blue energy exploded into a nearby table and the gun leapt out of the outlaws hand with the help of the hatchets blade, both of them pausing to watch as it skittered across the floor coming to land at the feet of few patrons who quickly backed away from it, wanting no part of this fight, both Warden and criminal turned back to regard each other.

Castigan was much broader and using that to his advantage slammed his palms into Corliss’s chest, knocking her back a few feet, giving him distance to fight.

“You won’t take me alive dirt born,” Castigan taunted, Corliss’s own smile growing wider “I really hoped you would say something like that” she growled her free hand disappearing behind her belt as it quickly produced an antique straight sword.

The dark mahogany handle lightly held in her hand a contrast to her pale skin as she flipped the blade, bringing it to a ready pose.

Patrons began to scatter, moving out of the way to give the two room. Ironically, she noticed, they did not leave the tavern, instead opting to stay and watch the events unfolding.

Castigan began circling her, favoring his right leg as the left dragged across the floor. Corliss nodded down to it “does it hurt Castigan, can you feel it before it rains, does it remind you of how much of an evil shit you are” Corliss taunted and the other man paused tilting his head to regard the Warden. “I think I will give you one to match Corliss, since after all you did me the honor of giving me this one” he finished nodding down to the leg.

Corliss rotated the hatchet, keeping the sword extended towards Castigan, every fiber of her body wanted to attack, wanted this man dead but she had a duty, a sworn oath to the crown to return him for trial and she would make good on that oath she vowed swallowing the anger that threatened to overtake her sanity at the thought of her friends broken and beaten body found not more than a week ago.

“Castigan, you can make this easy on yourself submit and come with me for trial, otherwise face the consequences” at that last statement she gripped the weapons tighter, taking a step towards the larger man.

The sneer that spread across his face was all the warning Corliss needed as he sprang at her, the hand he had put into the coat came out with a sword now arcing up hoping to catch the Warden by surprise, Corliss had been anticipating something like this and quickly dodged left.

As the sword swung up, Castigan not able to change its direction quickly enough as the blade passed by Corliss, so close she could feel the puff of wind as the metal tore through the air.

The Warden, easily dodging his attack drove the pick end of the hatchet into Castigan’s large biceps, while at the same time driving the tip of the sword into underside of the arm piercing the triceps.

Castigan let go of the sword his hand now useless, the sword hit the ground with a clatter, snatching back the arm, holding it close to his body. He hissed in pain, stepping back out of the reach of those deadly instruments the Warden carried. “I warned you” Corliss growled waiting to see what Castigan would do next.

The evil bastard might have been many things but stupid wasn’t one of them he looked over the situation and then lowered the dagger, dropping it to the floor.

“You can let me go Warden. I can make it worth your while…” Castigan began to say as another smile spread over his face.

Corliss matched it, hers displaying more malice “There is not enough gold in all the world Castigan,” she said.

His grin faded quickly, and with a burst of lightning-speed, he whipped a hand from behind his back as a small dagger he had palmed buried itself into her upper arm.

Corliss hissed looking down for a moment to see what damage had been done.

Using the distraction Castigan launched himself at her batting the sword blade away.

Not so disabled as I thought, she reflected, then he was on her slamming her to the ground his hand going into the back of his coat and producing yet another blade, this one the length of a machete as he brought it down towards Corliss’s neck.

Corliss quickly brought up the hatchet and winced as the loud clang of the two metal weapons slammed into each other close to her face. Pausing for a moment the hatchet slowly slid along Castigan’s blade as the man forced it further towards the Warden’s throat.

It made contact with the blades guard stopping the large knife just before it pierced the soft skin of her exposed neck and with one hand Corliss held it there.

Castigan pressing down on the weapon but he had lost a lot of blood and his exhaustion and handicap made it hard to gain the leverage he needed, but still he tried desperately to get the kill.

“Your dead Warden, your dead” Castigan kept repeating she could hear the strain as the man kept trying to push the weapon further towards her neck, towards her death.

She was a slight woman, but years of training and hunting had made her strong, however the weight of the large man was quickly becoming too much and she felt her arm begin to shake as the blade slowly advanced once again towards her neck.

Stretching out her wounded arm Corliss winced in pain. Her fingers reaching, dancing over the handle of the fallen hatchet that lay so close, the large blade inching further as it bit into the delicate skin of her neck.

She bit back the panic as her fingers refusing to get a purchase on the handle, she felt the blood begin to pool in the shallow wound around the blade as Castigan pushed harder trying to drive it those last few inches to her demise.

Corliss felt her fingers close around the hatchet and in one fell motion spun the blade and with a wide arc brought the weapon around and pierced Castigan’s neck driving the razor-sharp end just left of the large artery, pulling it out she did it again.

Each blow piercing nerve, muscle and soft tissue. With the third blow Corliss was rewarded as her opponent let go of the knife and slumped over from loss of blood and pain.

“Damn you Corliss, may Mephis shrivel your tits and rot your pussy” he spat into the Warden’s face, the sour smell of beer and meat causing her to wince at the smell. Corliss rolled him off of her with a grunt of effort and sat up wincing as she moved the wounded arm.

Two hours later the Warden was climbing up on to her horse, Castigan’s own horse behind her as she tied the reins to her own saddle, Corliss regarded the man, still out like a light from pain and blood loss, an old man shambled up poking at the fugitive as he continually shot an annoyed look to the Warden “What? Corliss asked annoyed, the old unkempt man simply grumbled and checked on Castigan.

"The bandages will hold as long as you are gentle, you will need to change them often to prevent infection, I assume since you had me patch him up you want him alive” the gravelly voice intoned giving the Warden a suspicious glance.

Corliss rolled her eyes and threw the man two coins. “Of course, I do doc, thank you for your ministrations I will do my best to ensure they weren’t wasted” Corliss finished and then with a nod shooed the man away, with a grumble he shambled into the inn.

Turning to the local sheriff Corliss nodded “Thank you for helping me put the bastard on the horse sheriff, he is in good hands now” she finished and with a nod he too retreated to the inn.

It was going to be a fun ride back she thought admiring her own rope skill. The large innkeeper was the last to approach coming out of the inn and walking over to Corliss. “Warden” he greeted her.

Corliss reached into a leather bag attached to her belt and threw the man down four gold sovereigns. “Master brock, I apologize for the damage to your inn and any injuries to your customers.” She finished and the Innkeeper smiled bowing slightly “May Aurtus grant you an uneventful trip” he finally said, turning and going back into his inn.

Castigan groaned behind her eliciting a smile from The Warden. Nodding at the patrons she rode out of the small town for the two-day ride back to the city that would deliver final justice to her prisoner. And another fugitive brought to justice, she thought smiling and nodding at the sour faces that stood along the few shops of the small village.

Most villagers were never happy to see Warden’s unless they were the victim of a crime. Even knowing this she smiled to each villager, nodding as she passed by. It wasn’t long until Corliss was beyond the fence and out into the territories.

Turning west she nudged the horse a little faster, hearing the grunts and moans from her prisoner as he lay lashed to his mount.

It was going to be a rough trip for poor Castigan she thought still smiling.

Listening, she caught the sound of hoofbeats approaching from the rear and Corliss’s smile widened as another horse pulled alongside of her.

“Apprentice Surin, you are not only late but I was forced to tress and place our fugitive onto the horse without you, would you like to explain to me where you were” Corliss stated forcing irritation into her tone and doing her best to hide a smile.

The exasperated teenager looked back at the town and then to his teacher and mistress, running a hand through the unruly mop of raven hair he sighed and then looked down at the ground “I’m so sorry Ghost, I was trying to get us supplies, but the shop keeper wanted to charge double because we are Wardens and said we could afford it, I told him that wasn’t fair and I wouldn’t pay double and then he said he wouldn’t sell any supplies to me, but I know we needed them so I argued with him, getting him down to one and a half of the cost, but then it took forever to load them into the packs and by the time I was done.

Well Warden you were already riding out” he blurted out and then with a wince waited for the chastising he was sure would follow his explanation. Corliss tilted her head back and laughed a deep belly laugh and then shaking her head and mumbling to herself urging her horse forward leaving the young apprentice confused and sitting there.

After a few moments the young man joined her “Um Ghost, what was that about?” he finally asked looking back at the town and then to Corliss.

“I am impressed Gorkin was able to get one and half out of you, I told him to try for three times, but I guess he felt bad for you” Corliss said conversationally.

It took the young man a few minutes before he finally put it together, at first not believing it, then as what had happened set in, he shot an irritated look at Corliss but quickly squashed it. “Mistress was this a training that I wasn’t supposed to know about, if so, did I pass,” the young man asked hopefully.

Corliss almost burst out into fresh laughter but instead repressed it. “No, young man. It’s called hazing the new guy, that’s all, Also a piece of advice, when in the company of civilians, call me Warden Corliss, Ghost is fine in private, but never around civilian’s” she finished and for a moment Surin was trying to figure out how to navigate respect with the irritation he so obviously felt.

Corliss decided to let him off the hook. “Surin, when I am not teaching you and we are just riding, if I irritate you just tell me.

One day you will be on this side of the situation and how you ask the apprentices to treat you reflects more on you than on them.

As for the hazing, relax we all go through it” she finished giving the young man a smile as they rode.

“Warden Corl.. er Ghost, I noticed your arm is wounded, we should stop so I can treat it” the young man said, and Corliss could hear the concern in his voice. Surin was a good kid, a gentle kid she still didn’t know if he was going to make a good Warden, but he would be a good man and that was the best raw material to start with.

“No, Surin, I will be fine it’s not that bad and the blood has stopped flowing so nothing critical was hit” Corliss answered him. She could tell the young man wasn’t happy about the answer, but he didn’t protest instead opting to ride in annoyed silence.

It took Corliss only a few minutes before she was tired of the quiet. “Surin, did I ever tell you how I ended up in the Warden’s?” she asked her apprentice the young man leaning forward on his horse and Corliss could hear the anticipation in his voice “NO Mistress, I mean I have heard stories, but you have never talked about it” he said barely hiding the interest in his tone.

Surin had only been riding with Corliss for a few weeks, before that he had spent the better part of five years in training and then working with three previous wardens before getting paired with Corliss for his final evaluation.

Uri had told her before she left for this hunt the kid would accompany her. Uri had high hopes for the young man, and it said something as this is the first time that Corliss had been paired with an apprentice.

She just wasn’t sure if it said good things about her or the kid or both. Uri was like that he enjoyed throwing curveballs to see how you would react to them. Sitting back, she regarded the young man, so exuberant and excited about his first hunt.

Though Corliss did not know why the Lord Adjudicator for the Wardens would have him go out after Castigan, he was incredibly dangerous which was one of the reasons she had ensured the shop keeper had kept young Surin busy while she was securing the fugitive.

If things had not gone her way the shopkeeper would have hid the young man until more Warden’s had arrived.

Corliss thanked the gods that wasn’t necessary. She put a smile on her face, she didn’t want to trouble the young man, but she would need to have a talk with Uri when she got back, the poor kid should have been sent on an easier assignment. Finally, turning to Surin who sat atop his horse waiting patiently “I was younger than you, probably about five years younger which would have made me twelve. My mother had died of fever and my father had left us years before, he had wanted a son, someone he could leave his legacy to, but instead he was given a bastard and a female one at that.

I fell in with local gangs in the capital and one day I was picking the pocket of a brutish looking fellow and he caught me” Corliss began smiling as she remembered that day well, it was the day that changed her life forever and made her what she was today.

“Instead of turning me in, the barbarian took me in and made me his apprentice, his name was Uri Ammital, though you know him as the Lord Adjudicator” Corliss continued, she could see the young man lean closer to her, enraptured by the tale which she was sure had been told to him many times as a young apprentice, most did get told the tale of Corliss and her misadventures with Uri.

“Uri taught me everything I know; he was an amazing teacher and took me under his wing for many years until the day I took the vows” she finished still smiling at the thought of the man.

Though Uri had been more than a teacher, he had been like a father to Corliss when she had needed one most, following in his footsteps had been easy Corliss had worshipped the man and everything he stood for.

“Uri once told me that one person can make a difference, one person can change the course of history should they be brave enough to stand in the way of destiny” she stated.

“Ma’am, uh…Ghost” the young man corrected, and Corliss waved a dismissive hand. “As I said Surin, when we ride, I am Ghost, not Maam or Mistress or even Warden” she finished getting a smile of relief from the young man. “Yes Ma-, I mean Ghost” he corrected with a sheepish grin on his face.

“Is it true Lord Ammital taught you to be a master brawler and a master swordsman by the time you were sixteen?” he asked hesitantly, and Corliss chuckled. “I see old Vegram has been telling stories while getting you to work in the kitchen,” she said, shaking her head.

“Yes, it is true” she finally finished the young man seemed to be exploding out of his saddle “Corliss, that’s amazing, “he gushed and Corliss waved him off.

“Mastering the martial combat arts is not the hardest thing you will do as a Junior Warden, but it does require you to learn and master multiple ancient forms of fighting,” she finished, and Surin nodded, taking the advice to heart.

Every young initiate worried they would not be able to handle the fugitives and that they would fail in the eyes of their teacher Corliss knew but also knew that Uri wouldn’t send someone out unless he was absolutely sure they were ready.

They continue to ride in silence for a while, Corliss thinking of why Uri would send this young man on a hunt like this, that wasn’t like him and to think of it she had never recalled an initiate being paired with a Warden on anything more than a simple courier mission or court appearance. This bothered her and Corliss didn’t know if the old man was testing her or Sorin.

Uri didn’t do anything without a reason and everything he did was a test meant to test one or both people participating that much she knew.

“Ghost,” Surin asked tentatively she was going to have to help the kid work on his assertiveness she thought wincing as he called for her again. “What is it Surin” she finally answered

“How hard is it to follow the living oath, I mean do you ever wish you hadn’t taken it?” he finally asked and Corliss nodded this was a question every initiate eventually asked hell she had even asked it of Uri.

“I will first tell you what Lord Ammital told me the first time I asked him that question. The Wardens are the line between anarchy and law in the land, there is no other and if the Wardens ceased to be then the country would descend into throws of lawlessness” she started remembering when she had been given this speech.

Unlike today she thought, pulling her coat tighter ebbing the chill of the cold autumn air as she thought back to a warm summer day when a much younger Corliss had asked her master and the head of the order about the oath.

“The oath is the bond between the monarchy and the people, it is the trust that is placed into the hands of men and women to stand up against the evil in this world to ensure the victims get the justice they deserve” she repeated to Surin as she herself heard the words over a decade ago.

“Surin, when we take the oath, we do agree to not get married, or have children. We agree to make justice our partner in life and that is not for everyone, but I will tell you there is no higher calling young man, but that does not mean you give up sex” she finished shooting a smile at the apprentice as his face turned beat red “yes Warden” he whispered but refusing to meet her eyes.

They continued to ride for a while, Corliss thinking over the young man’s frustration, she couldn’t blame him she too had felt the same way at his age, but Uri, well-being Uri was not always the best person to talk to “Trust your Training” was his motto and answer for everything.

Shaking it off, Corliss looked over to the young man, was it her she wondered or were the apprentices getting younger and younger, dismissing the thought the Senior Warden cleared her throat to get his attention.

“Surin, have you practiced much with your SenPai, aside from the initial training?” She asked and watched as the young man’s face lit up.

Every apprentice relished the moment they were able to learn to use the SenPai she thought suppressing a smile as the young apprentice answered excitement edging his voice “Not really Warden” he said reaching up and exposing the long leather bracer that was strapped to his left arm.

Corliss looked over to see the worn leather bracer and smiled as the sunlight danced over the multicolored runes that had been carved from crystal and inlaid into the leather as the young man ran his fingers over them, the runes beginning to glow slightly as he summoned the power within them.

“Slow down there Surin, let’s go over what you know before we start using it” she said and watched as his face fell a little, the young man pushing the sleeve back down to cover the magical bracer.

“So, what do you know about the SenPai Apprentice?” Corliss asked continuing to regard the young man. He did his best to hide the eye roll, but she still caught it and suppressed another smile. “The SenPai was commissioned by the first Emperor for the Warden’s, it was crafted by the first members of the Order of the Dragon after signing the Agreement” he recited as dry as if it were directly quoted from the textbook.

Time to throw him off a bit, she thought. “Okay, how is it Wardens can use Magic? Are we Mages?” she asked and could see another half-suppressed eye roll.

“No. Wardens are not Mages nor do we wield Magic, that is the realm of the Mage and the Order, however like everyone we all descend from those with power so we have the ability to draw on power to a minor degree, but we do not have the ability to actually use it directly, that is where the Senpai comes in” he stated almost bored.

Corliss had to suppress a laugh. “Okay, then how does the SenPai work?” she asked watching as the question caught him off guard, Corliss could see his mind working, it was not an easy question, Wardens did not know the finer points of Magic or Runic script so she waited patiently as Surin struggled to form an answer.

He started and then stopped for a moment forming his thoughts and she could hear the struggle in his words as he finally started to answer the question “The SenPai is a set of runic spells that the Warden can activate giving them abilities such as increased hearing and sight as well as activation of the Spirit Bond” he said and Corliss watched the smile form on his face, he was proud of his answer and she had to agree, it was accurate.

“What is the spirit bond, Surin?” Corliss asked and could see the young man’s face fall. “We are able to identify with a creature, something that mirror’s our own values and strengths, that animal is amplified and made real through the spell of the SenPai, giving the Warden a friend in combat and a scout in tracking” he finished and his smile grew wider, again he had done well and Corliss conceded the young man had learned well.

“Okay then, let’s see how you do” she said and Surin’s face brightened as he pushed the sleeve up, running his fingers once more over the worn leather and crystal runes on the hand me down bracer.

SenPai’s were always passed down from one warden to the next she thought, remembering when she had received her own during the ceremony of change, where an old Warden retires and a new one takes their place.

Corliss watched as the young man began to touch the runes lighting them in sequence as he closed his eyes his fingers continued to dance over the bracer as energy formed next to him, a ball of blue light coalesced into existence and formed into a large horned owl. The creature was pure energy as if someone had taken blue light and drawn the owl over the world.

Taking flight, the animal began to circle the two of them, Corliss watched impressed at the young man’s skill in calling forth his spirit bond.

Opening his eyes Surin looked over at the large creature as it circled and smiled at the Warden.

With a nod of approval, she returned the smile “Now send him out and tell me what’s around us” Corliss said and with a nod Surin closed his eyes and sent the command to the owl.

With an almost instantaneous reaction the creature lifted further into the air, floating over the currents as it made its way out towards the distant woods. She watched as Surin opened his eyes, his normal earnest blue eyes had been replaced with white orbs as he now saw through the spirit bond.

It was unsettling to see and left the Warden vulnerable to attack while in this state. “The woods go for many miles; I see a small farm town to the east and a trade road with a little market traffic heading towards a larger town in the north” he said almost dreamily.

Corliss nodded in approval “Very good Surin, that should be enough for today” she finished and watched as he closed his eyes, dismissing the animal as the bracers glow began to fade. “Yes Warden” he said pulling down the sleeve and shaking his head clear.

It was quite an experience when merging with the spirit bond and one that sometimes took a moment to come back from, she thought.

They rode for two days Corliss telling stories and Surin listening intently until finally the stone wall of Lores crested the hill giving them visual confirmation that their journey was at an end.

Like the few other bigger cities in the kingdom the defenses were housed in stone instead of wood. Brushing her hand along her own SenPai the runes lit up as her eyes began to glow, her vision jumping across the mile distance as if she herself were now standing directly in front of the town.

She studied the walls and the guard towers as well as the four energy cannons, the large crystal tipped contraptions that were meant to take out siege engines and not people, at least that was the excuse for needing them she thought wincing as the memory of what those would do to a person passed through her mind. Closing her eyes, she allowed the energy to dissipate, and her eyes dimmed as her vision returned to normal.

They rode to the gate where four Royal guards stood sentry in their black tunics with the gold lioness, the mark of the Empress emblazoned across the front. Corliss nodded to them, the guard might be the security in the city but the justice in the kingdom came from the Wardens and even these guards knew it.

Corliss pulled her glove off and extended the hand showing the silver ring with the head of a Griffon, its two red ruby eyes glittering in the sun. The badge of office for the Wardens, it was a badge that showed their authority.

The guard examined it carefully and then checked on the prisoner, he was out like a light Corliss would love to tell them it was because she hit the man so hard. But that wasn’t the truth, anytime she caught an unruly fugitive she had a small liquid she would put on their skin. It kept them sleeping and as long as you didn’t administer too much, they would wake up once it wore off with a slight headache and usually in a cell.

With the young initiate traveling with her Corliss wasn’t taking any chances and ensured her prisoner slept the entire trip. “You may enter Warden Corliss, you will need to stop at the Messengers house next to Aurtus Keep, there is a message waiting there for you, it came in a few days ago from Warden’s Castle, it was marked urgent” the guard finished and motioned them to enter the city.

A message waiting for her she wondered, and a chill ran up her spine, it was not a good sign she reflected. They rode down the main street connecting the gate to the keep.

They passed stone row houses with colorful signs hanging above the doors the two making their way to the center of town and stopping in front of Aurtus Keep, the church like all the others in cities and towns doubled as the town center, town offices and the church. Upon riding up an old bald man with a genuine smile came hurrying out of the old stone keep greeting them.

Corliss smiled at the old man “Hail, Messenger Kolpin, it is good to see you again my friend” Corliss called. The old man was short and carried a little extra weight on his mid-section, enough so it was noticeable even through the oversized brown robes that all messengers wore. Stopping short on the walk brown eyes twinkled with humor as they appraised the two Wardens.

“It is very good to see you my friend and I see you brought us one of our favorite tenants for the city Jail the old man said smiling at his own joke. The large wooden double doors opened, and two guards exited to come stand next to the messenger. Corliss noted the same black tunics with the gold Lioness, Empress guards she affirmed. The Messenger motioned to the trussed-up Castigan who was now just starting to stir. “Take our guest here and place him in the cells, he will be tried in the morning” Messenger Kolpin ordered and the two moved to accommodate the old man. “Will you be staying to witness the trial? I assure you it will be a short one,” Kolpin said, eyeing the man, the Messenger didn’t even try to hide the hostility in that gaze.

Corliss knew that this man had killed more than one of the people that Kolpin called friends. “I am not sure, I was told you have a letter for me” she asked and immediately Kolpin affirmed it by nodding his head and reaching up one of the overly large sleeves on the robe and producing a piece of paper with a large red wax seal.

Corliss didn’t even have to look she knew the stamp would feature a Griffon’s head. Kolpin handed it, he turned to Surin, the poor man was practically falling over with exhaustion in his saddle. “Surin, feed the horses and then go get us rooms at the inn, once you finish with that, please get some sleep. I will join you later for dinner I need to take care of this and do some errands” Corliss said and the young man shook his head gratefully.

Corliss stepped down off her horse and Surin took them away, heading for the stables “What did you do to that poor boy Corliss, he looks beaten to death, poor child Kolpin said shooting a withering gaze at Corliss.

“Just because they are volunteer initiates, does not mean you can try to kill them. Corliss put her hands up and put on her “I’m innocent look. I did nothing. He volunteered for night watch twice, my friend. Who was I to argue with him?” she finished.

Kolpin smiled shaking his head. “Okay, if he was that stupid, then maybe he deserves his exhaustion.”

Corliss laughed the two walking into the large stone church, Kolpin left the warden in his quarters while he went to secure the prisoner and make arrangements for the trial the next day.

Corliss looked down at the letter in her hand.

Uri didn’t send irrelevant notes, so whatever this was, was important Corliss knew that, but she didn’t know if she wanted to know what was in it. After a moment of arguing with herself she winced and broke the seal. Carefully unfolding the parchment, she began to read the familiar handwriting of her friend and mentor.

The letter was incredibly short and to the point. It simply said, ‘Get Back to the castle as fast as you can – Uri’

Corliss sighed. She was going to have to disappoint both Kolpin and Surin, she could neither stay nor could she allow the young man the night to recuperate.

With a shake of her head she walked out of the messenger’s quarters and quickly found Kolpin surrounded by what looked like older farmers and shop keepers must be the town elders Corliss thought, waiting respectfully, just outside of earshot to the group until Kolpin had finished.

As the group broke up, she stepped over to her friend. “I am going to have to leave you my friend, I have been called back to the castle on business, Kolpin’s face fell as he regarded his friend. “I’m sorry Corliss, I hope everything is okay” he said, and Corliss nodded “Just work” she responded and then embraced her friend.

“Make sure that bastard gets the justice he deserves Kolpin, I mean it, the guy is an animal” Corliss finished and walked out of the church to find her assistant and ruin his plans as well.

The two of them were packed and riding out within the hour, poor Surin looked like he was ready to fall off his horse.

Corliss urged her horse a little faster, she didn’t like the note only twice had she ever received a note similar during a retrieval of a fugitive and neither time was it good news. The two rode for the rest of the day finally making camp an hour before sunset mostly because her poor initiate had damn near fallen twice as he could barely stay awake.

Corliss took watch allowing the young man some much-needed sleep. She had spent the last year going from one mission to another, bringing in fugitive after fugitive Corliss had developed a reputation for getting the job done.

Corliss smiled she liked the rep, though she would never admit it to anyone else she reflected thinking of some of the more difficult chases she had been on.

“Corliss, why do you think we were called back so suddenly, I mean I have never heard of someone being recalled so soon after a successful catch” Sorin asked from under his blanket, he had slept a few hours but Corliss could see the bloodshot and bleary eyes of the young man staring up at her.

She wouldn’t admit to him that was exactly what was bothering her you had to be careful how much frustration you showed around the initiates, sometimes they would get the wrong idea.

Corliss loved her calling, because it was more than a career, it was a calling. She wasn’t drawn to the catch or even the hunt she enjoyed the faces of the victims when they came to watch the criminal pay the price for their crime.

A lot of times they didn’t think these people would, that they would disappear into the wilderness never to be heard from again.

When Corliss dragged them back to civilization and to the town from whence, they came the looks of amazement, gratitude and relief made this worth it. But there were times that the politics and the business of what she did got in the way, when they pushed too hard because of her success as they tried to lobby the Empress for more money or resources and Corliss would be raised on a pedestal and shown as the hero of the Wardens, stories would circulate about her achievements and successes.

He thought this might be one of those times and how do you explain to the kid what that means without killing his enthusiasm Corliss thought looking at the bleary but excited young man who reminded Corliss a lot of herself and how Uri must had seen her all those years ago. “There are a lot of things that we have to do aside from just catching the bad guys sometimes those things are not as much fun, but still necessary so this is probably one of those, get some sleep we will find out tomorrow.” Corliss finished and watched as the young man nestled into his sleeping bag and before long was quickly snoring away.

She sat there listening to him for most of the night, once in a while closing her eyes but only sleeping lightly a trick that Uri had taught her while they were on hunts. It was one that was hard to break and honestly, she couldn’t think of the last time she got a good night sleep.

Hell, she couldn’t remember a time when she wasn’t out on a hunt she realized with some surprise.

The sun rose over the trees casting shadows on the skeletal wood of the forest now that fall had fully settled in, it gave the forest a dead look, now that brown had overtaken the normal lush green of summer and spring, a rustling came from behind her as Surin began to stir and collect himself, a quick breakfast of salted pork jerky greeted him as he joined the Warden Surin finishing his pork and checking that the waterskins still had ample supply in them.

The sun had finally cleared the tops of the trees but not enough to warm the air she thought closing her oversize leather coat around her body and wincing as the chilled air bit at her exposed skin. Corliss stopped to watch the sky smiling at the burst of color, as if someone had touched up it up using a brush of light pink.

She could see her breath but that would go away once the chill of early morning passed until then she just put up with it instead of covering her face with the leather half mask that hung permanently around her neck.

Surin cleaned up the camp, packing up the horses and preparing to move out. Something about the way the request had been worded was bothering her as she watched the young apprentice finish his tasks.

They rode straight through until almost evening, only stopping to rest the horses once during the day as they crested the last hill a smile crossed the Wardens face, the silhouette of Warden castle coming into view, the large stone complex nestled snugly into the side of the large mountain that shared the castles name.

It was a well-fortified place and had once been used by an Emperor who ruled over the entire coast, until his death two hundred years ago. The keep had been willed to them by the emperor and so far, the crown had honored the request, every so often a rumor would start that the crown wanted it for some summer palace. But as it is with rumors, aside from a bit of emotional angst, nothing ever happened.

Corliss just chalked it up to those who liked to mix it up and cause a bit of drama, either because they were bored or because they enjoyed being the center of attention as was the case when they told these yarns. The mountain was a steep granite face and Corliss noticed the beginnings of winter appearing as light snow covering the rocks and outcroppings. The way was dangerous if you didn’t know the trail.

But Corliss had been doing this trip since she was a young girl and knew every single turn, bend and dip the two making it up to the castles main entrance in very little time. The entrance was a large planked drawbridge that nestled into a twenty-foot keystone arch. The appearance making the castle very intimidating.

They rode into the main yard of Warden Castle as they navigated the normal crowds of initiates and Wardens preparing for trips, training or performing various maintenance tasks assigned during downtime.

“Hail Corliss” came a call and she looked up to see a young man with long raven-colored hair in the leather brown cuirass of an initiate as he came running over to greet the two as they approached the stable.

“Miren, how goes it my friend, have they assigned you a new Warden?” Corliss asked. She had trained Miren in the arts of tracking and in doing so he had become like a little brother to her.

Miren shook his head. “Not yet, but apparently a bunch of the initiates are going down to Toren, a note came in and something is going on down there. I think that is why they called you back, Ghost.” the young man said. Corliss listened and didn’t let the smile on her face change, but inside her stomach dropped. Galen had requested her she thought nodding to the young initiate as he guided his horse into the stable.

The stables had been around as long as the keep itself and it was a good balance of stone and wood, though most of the wood had been replaced over the years. The stable could hold nearly fifty horses in their own paddocks. As Corliss rode down the main thoroughfare of the stables, she spotted the large mountain of a man that ran the old stables. “Corliss, you had better not run that mare into the ground, or I will take it out of your damn hide, Aurtus is my witness” he yelled coming over to them.

Corliss smiled jumping down off the beautiful beast and handing the reins to the massive bearded man. He motioned and two initiates appeared from literally nowhere to guide the horses deeper into the stables. “She was a dream Vim, rode well and behaved herself” she said clapping him on the back.

The smile faltered a little on Vim’s face “Uri is looking for you, I would go see him before you unpack” he said, and Corliss nodded.

Turning to her young initiate “Sorin, go unpack and rest for a bit, I think we will be here for a bit so this is always a good time to ensure your rested should we get sent out quickly” she said and the young man nodded enthusiastically and then bolted for the main castle building.

The two looked on after him smiling. “Ahh, remember being that young my friend” Vim mused and Corliss just shook her head “Hell Vim, I don’t think we were ever that young” this elicited a deep belly laugh from the bigger man who clapped Corliss on the back, nearly causing her to lose balance. She left the stable walking up the main stairs and entering into the castle proper.

The large entrance had quite probably seen its share of important guests, the entire structure meant to intimidate and make those visiting feel small and insignificant next to the grand entrance and main staircase.

Most of the ornate wall hangings that had been rumored to cover the old stone arches and walls had long ago been removed instead stag heads and weapons were prominently displayed along both of the staircases.

And over the walls the large mahogany spiral stairs wound up on each side of the entryway. Once the emperor had come down one of these sides greeting dignitaries and other important guests.

Nowadays, the stairs crawled with initiates and wardens going about various tasks. It was the heart of the large keep, the main arteries that pumped life and activity through the old building and on any given day over a hundred people used them in their daily activities.

Corliss snapped herself out of her reverie opting to take the left staircase as it seemed less busy this day. She climbed up the wood staircase making her way around initiates carrying boxes of weapons and clothing as well as food and other assorted items bound for who knew where.

As she made her way down the long hall that ran the entire length of the castle the traffic fell off so that as she neared one end, she was the only one in the hallway.

The maroon carpet though worn was still a credit to the craftsmanship of days gone she thought. Finally coming to stand outside of a large set of double doors.

She stood for a moment outside and collected her thoughts, the room having once been a second dining room had become Uri’s office since he had taken over as the Lord Adjudicator.

Slamming her fist against the old wood she could hear the echoes of the knock making its way through the room. “Come in” came the familiar booming voice from the other side of the door.

Corliss pushed at the door, though the aged wood took a few attempts, the edge catching on the frame and holding the door fast, after a few good heaves, it finally succumbed to her shoulder and moved, guided by the well-oiled iron hinges that held it.

Opening the door, she walked into the long rectangular room, one side covered in a large table with cities and other carved wooden icons that represented various missions, buildings or people or places of interest.

Corliss had always liked the board, Uri said it let me him see the big picture of their work and allowed for a better strategic picture of the territories.

Corliss didn’t know if he was correct, she just knew it looked cool. She thought about this conversation as she made her way further into the cavernous office.

Uri Ammital was a large bear of a man; hell, his beard alone could supply hair for half the castle Corliss thought suppressing a smile. He stood stooped over what was once the large dining table eyeing it as he moved pieces over the wooden carved relief of the area. It was a detailed carving meant to depict the rises, valleys and farm fields of the territory.

Uri had always used it when dealing with massive hunts for those few fugitives that eluded capture. The fact that he stood there now eyeing the large table did not bode well for the conversation

Corliss thought wincing slightly as she approached the large table and the even larger man concentrating on its contents. Approaching she could see the cold grey eyes assessing every movement of his pieces. Old Iron eyes was the nickname he had been given at a fairly young age and damn it if it isn’t true she thought no one wanted to be under the scrutinizing gaze of Uri much less the subject of his anger. He had a legendary temper according to some rumors but Corliss herself had never actually seen it.

It was said that Uri once threw a house Lord out of a window during an argument while trying to bind his eldest son for murder.

Corliss thought the rumor was crap, but then again, anything is possible she thought. Corliss approached the table those iron eyes turning, once they took in the sight of her Uri brightened. Since taking her under his wing the big man had become like a father to Corliss. More than her own had if she was being honest with herself.

“Cor, I hear the mission went well, how did our young initiate do?” Uri asked in his resounding baritone that had more often than not scared some unwary initiate into line.

Corliss smiled “Well aside from why you sent an unproven initiate on what we knew would be a dangerous retrieval, it went fine. I am still not comfortable with that decision, but it was yours to make” she said acceding to the other man’s authority. Uri nodded and his face transformed into a somber expression. “It’s getting harder to find initiates willing to serve, I don’t know if you have noticed but our ranks are rather thin these past few years.

We have lost five Wardens in the last six months alone and we need to bolster our ranks as quickly as possible. If your assessment is good, I am going to fast track Surin and a few others now instead of a year from now” Uri explained, and Corliss frowned at the thought of this.

She knew about the losses but they had so far handled it fine, she and a few others had more work but nothing they had not been able to handle, What wasn’t Uri telling her she wondered the look on the man’s face seemed serene but she had known the old bear for many years and she could see the lack of sleep and deep-set worry in those eyes.

“Okay, it’s your call,” she simply said. If Uri wants to talk about it, he will. Never a good idea to push the old man, she thought dropping the discussion. Internally she thought of the preparations she had seen just coming into the keep, a lot of supplies were being stored as well as weapons stocked into the armories more so than usual.

What were they preparing for she wondered? But those were things for later, she had been called back and urgently for a reason. “Why did you send the letter, I assume there is something that requires my attention” she stated looking around the room and noticing the stacks of maps and documents, most of them sporting the broken seal of the palace.

So, he has been in communications with the Empress, interesting.

“Because you personally have been requested, Lord Seer Galen Bor requires your presence. Corliss’s thoughts were quickly interrupted as she snapped her head back to look at the Leader of the Wardens. “Why would Lord Bor need my expertise, surely he has people” Corliss stated but it was hard to hide the hostility in her voice and Uri winced as Corliss finished her bile-filled statement. “Look Cor, I can send someone else, I can simply tell him you were not available” Uri said gently. “With your… history I would understand if you wanted to skip this one” Uri continued.

Corliss honestly thought about taking the old man up on his offer. She couldn’t imagine Galen would have any need of her at all.

“No” she finally answered trying to keep the hostility from her words “I will go, anything we have on the mission other than the request?” she asked reverting to her professionalism to mask the personal loathing she held for the Lord.

Uri shook his head “Are you going to be able to keep yourself in check, or should I send someone with you?” he asked Uri laughed but Corliss could tell he wasn’t joking he was worried his protégé would wind up in prison by doing something stupid like punching a self-important pompous lord.

Corliss shook her head “I will be fine, if he has a job and this isn’t some trick to reach out, we can work together, I will do my best not to hit the man, after all he is my father” Corliss stated and again Uri winced. “He only sent some basic information, The Empress is searching for a fugitive, a mage and it is critical that he is found fast, he is a stranger to these parts but they have been unable to locate him” Uri said and Corliss shook her head “Sounds more like a missing person Uri, why are we looking for a mage and one without crimes against him, I assume anyway since no list of crimes came with the request” she finished flipping through the leather-bound stack of documents that Uri had handed to her.

Uri looked bothered “What is it?” Corliss asked cocking her head as she assessed the older man. After a moment he shook it off. “Nothing, just it seems odd the Empress is mounting the Wardens for something like this” he finally said clapping Corliss on the back. With a nod he turned and headed for the door.

“Don’t kill your father Corliss, I don’t want to attend your execution” Uri called after her.

Corliss just laughed “You would have to catch me first old man” she taunted, and the door closed behind her as she walked out into the bustling hall of the castle. “Preparations indeed” she whispered as he saw the initiates carrying boxes, weapons and other things with a purpose to the various storerooms of the keep. Uri was definitely planning something and keeping it close to the vest she thought.

Corliss made her way down the main steps avoiding the line of initiates as she made her way deeper into the castles first floor. The large dining and living quarters spread out along the hall she walked down. The crystal lanterns set low allowing her to see but not too bright as to ruin her night vision.

Something Uri had done all his life that had made its way into the daily routine of all Wardens. Turning into the last entrance of the hall she came to a desk cluttered with paperwork in the foreground of a room busting with boxes and cloth bags. The quartermaster was ancient, he had been ancient when Corliss was still an initiate but yet the man still lived and not only that still worked in the castle.

She honestly believed the old man would be here long after Corliss herself had retired. “What can I do for you young Warden” the scratchy voice asked as the hunched figure came out from around the desk. What little hair he had hung out in white tufts, his lips wrapped around his gums as the teeth that would have supported them had long ago been removed.

“Master Venson, it is always good to see you sir, I need to requisition supplies for a month” Corliss said smiling at the old man.

He shambled over eyeing her suspiciously before holding out his hand. Corliss looked blankly at it for a moment before she remembered the stack of paperwork Uri had handed her. “Sorry” She said with a sheepish grin as rifling through the items until she found the proper document. Uri always had the Warden’s package ready to go and pretty much left it open-ended for them to requisition the supplies they thought they would need.

Venson didn’t even argue anymore, taking the paper and scratching out the number of items needed before he called back into the stacks. After a moment something crashed far back in the room and a lanky young man came scrambling out from among the old wooden shelves. “Boy, if you broke something, I will take it out of your hide” Venson called to him as he ran forward brandishing the cane he rarely used at the young man.

The boy came running up stopping just in front of the much smaller Venson. “I’m sorry master, I swear, nothing broke, I will clean it up momentarily” the young man excitedly blurted, from his eyeing of the cane Corliss guessed it wouldn’t be the first time he had been hit with it. Venson remembered he had customers and eyed Corliss before putting down the wooden stick of doom as she had heard more than one Initiate call it.

“Get this together and meet Warden Corliss in the stable,” he said, shoving the paper into his chest.

The young man smiled his blue eyes lighting up under the mop of unkempt blonde hair as he shook his head enthusiastically. “Of course, sir, mistress. I will be there momentarily,” he said and then sailed back into the racks of supplies.

Corliss shook her head and smiled, she too had fallen under the old man’s tutelage for a time and she did not recall it fondly at all. But she had survived it like so many before and after and had developed a true appreciation for the logistics it took to run the castle in the process.

“I will take my leave Quartermaster. I anticipate the young man’s arrival” Corliss said getting an irritated eye from Venson who rose the cane slightly off the floor.

Corliss turned and left before the old man could remind Corliss of what it felt like to be smacked by it. True to his word the young initiate came running into the stable thirty minutes later carrying the heavy leather bag of supplies, the thing was wider than he was, and the poor kid swayed as he tried to make a straight line to Corliss’s stable pen.

“Here give that to me,” Corliss said, grunting as she hefted the month of supplies. “Thank you, Warden Corliss, I better get back before he decides I need a reminder of punctuality” he said turning not seeing the wince that elicited from Corliss, remembering all too well what that lesson felt like. Breaking down the bulky bag of supplies she began to carefully pack them in the pockets and satchel areas of the saddle and butt pack on the large beast. Though she knew that she would quite probably leave the animal at the keep when she began hunting.

It was nice to have the supplies so she could pick and choose based on the situation she thought.

On her back, tied with a thick piece of leather hung the straight sword that had saved her against Castigan the matching mahogany sheath and handle made it almost look like a staff. But it was the Bor family sword. The only thing her father had ever given her. Aside from her hatchets, it was one of the few weapons she carried with her everywhere.

It had been crafted by a great-great-grandfather; a Chinese man who decided the family needed a traditional weapon. It was decorated with old and worn Chinese dragons and metal swirls giving it a very oriental look. The sword was well made and still served the Warden well despite not being the standard bastard sword that every Warden carried.

One of the few perks of knowing the boss well she smiled, climbing onto her horse, grabbing the pack animals' reins and heading out of the stables. She rode out of the castle and began the two-day trek to Galen’s keep. As she made her way under the large keystone, the hollow sound of the hoofs beating against the wooden bridge reassuring and she smiled, but it was quick lived as Corliss caught sight of six master wardens standing in a line high above on the stone wall of the Keep.

Pausing the horse she regarded them, she could see the tell-tale signs that they were on recon, each one with a hand on the SenPai, eyes white and distant. Why would Uri have Wardens on guard she wondered a sliver of worry piercing her calm as she nudged the horse forward.
